# Finding Angle STR

## Setting Up the Triangle

In triangle PQR, I know two angles:
- ∠P = 40°
- ∠Q = 35°

So the third angle is:
$$\angle R = 180° - 40° - 35° = 105°$$

## Using the Parallel Lines

Since $\overline{ST} \parallel \overline{QR}$ and point T lies on segment PR, I can treat line PR as a **transversal** cutting the two parallel lines.

The **corresponding angles** are equal:
$$\angle PTS = \angle PRQ = 105°$$

## Finding Angle STR

Since T lies on segment PR (between P and R), the rays $\overrightarrow{TP}$ and $\overrightarrow{TR}$ are **opposite rays** along line PR. Therefore:

$$\angle STR = 180° - \angle PTS = 180° - 105° = 75°$$

$$\boxed{75}$$
